constraints: Comparison sorting has worst-case Θ(n log n) time.

blocks.text: Copying n records costs Θ(n), the one comparison sort costs Θ(n log n), and q worst-case binary searches cost q × Θ(log n) = Θ(q log n). Their sum is Θ(n + n log n + q log n) = Θ(n log n + q log n), matching the offered time bound. The retained defensive copy contains n records, establishing Θ(n) extra space.

O(q n log n) re-sorts for every query instead of reusing one copy. O(n + q) omits both comparison sorting and logarithmic searches. O(n² + q) replaces the independent query term and uses a loose quadratic preprocessing bound. Space is not O(1) or O(log n) because the complete n-record copy remains stored.

blocks.text: Counting sort avoids comparison lower bounds by indexing a bounded discrete domain. Its work and memory include the range size k, so O(n + k) can be worse than comparison sorting when k is enormous. The assumption must therefore appear in the problem and cost model. This is the transfer boundary behind legitimate linear sorting claims: declare the algorithm, key representation, and range rather than generalizing from the word sort.
